$comment: EXP-1537 (Android first, EXP-1522 / #1546): what a SEND leaves in THE composer ×4 (web `components/session-composer.tsx` + `hooks/use-launch-composer.ts`, desktop `ui::steer_viewer` + `ui::agent_screen` + `ui::chat_screen`, iOS `SessionComposerCard` + `AgentComposerModel`, Android `AgentSessionViewModel` + `AgentScreen`'s launch; EXP-1543 the issue COMMENT composers ×4 too: web `components/comment-composer.tsx` (the bottom composer and the reply under a card), desktop `ui::timeline` (bottom + reply), iOS `IssueDetailBottomBar`, Android `CommentRepliesViewModel`, an attachments-only comment included); model = pure `composerAfterSend(input)` (src/composer-send.ts; desktop `domain::composer_send`, iOS ExpCore `ComposerSend.swift`, Android `domain/ComposerSend.kt`), every mirror replays `cases` and compares the WHOLE expected object. #FEED-237: a composer bound to a SESSION (sessionId) clears at the press instead and its message becomes an outbox bubble (message-delivery.json); these rules hold for every other composer (the launch composer that starts a chat, the comment composers). THE FIELD OWNS ITS TEXT: it stays editable while a send is in flight (the uploads, then `sessions.send`), so the user may keep typing, add or remove attachments. `sent` = the field's text EXACTLY as it was when Send was pressed (before any trim; the wire carries the trimmed copy) and the ids of the attachments that went out; `current` = the field and its attachments when the send settles. `outcome` `sent` (the server took it): the text clears ONLY if the field still equals `sent.text` byte for byte, else the field keeps everything as it is now (nothing is cut out of an edited field: the user sees what was sent in the transcript); every attachment that went out leaves, one added meanwhile stays, `current` order kept. `outcome` `failed` (an upload or the send refused; a toast says so): the field and its attachments stay exactly as they are now. A command the client runs itself (`/effort`) and a slash command follow the same rule. A SEND OUTLIVES ITS SCREEN: backing out, switching chats or closing the view never cancels the uploads or the send (it runs on a scope that outlives the view); when the screen is gone the rule applies to the draft that survives it (Android's steer connection, iOS `AgentSessionModel`; a comment composer that moved on to another issue keeps its new draft) and is a no-op where the field died with the view (web, desktop, the iOS chat and app-editor drafts).
